source.version_note: Published Synthese 201(1), article 21, online 7 January 2023. Received 9 June 2022 and accepted 4 December 2022. The 2022 DOI suffix does not contradict 2023 publication.
source.verification_method: All seventeen supplied pages, all footnotes and bibliography read. File inspection finds no substantive figures/tables; rendered pages 10, 11 and 13 verify the risk typo, control-gap definition and Tesla footnote. Publisher/Crossref verify identity/date. Targeted primary NTSB findings and public automation-taxonomy descriptions check technical examples without claiming a full standard or independent crash investigation.

citation.title: The risks of autonomous machines: from responsibility gaps to control gaps

reading.source_scope_note: Conceptual moral-philosophy argument comparing responsibility remainders, counterfactual deficits, blameless harm, indirect blame and risk-control requirements. No experiment, systematic evidence synthesis, calibrated risk threshold or validated intervention is reported.
access_limits: All seventeen text pages, conceptual definitions, equations/inequalities, footnotes, declarations and bibliography read. No substantive statistical figures or tables are present.

No public supplement/data-availability link found in the inspected main PDF/publisher page. No raw data, code, preregistration or independently fully read cited philosophical book was obtained; this paper reports an argument rather than a new dataset.

The full substantive 21 October 2021 NTSB press update and selected portions of the final HIR-23-02 report, notably its crash/driver/Autopilot analysis on printed page 8 and date on page 1, were read for the Tesla correction. The complete 13-page report and its figures/docket were not independently fully reviewed.

SAE J3016 public indexed abstract states six levels, 0–5; direct SAE access returned a JavaScript/robot verification page. NHTSA’s public automated-vehicle page was inspected as additional context. The full licensed standard and current approval law were not read or used for legal advice.
No author contact, external message, participant-data access, source-code execution, real vehicle test or private-link retrieval occurred.

study.type: Normative/conceptual argument with hypothetical autonomous-car and kitchen-appliance cases. No sample, measured effect, safety certification or demonstrated closure of a real control gap.
study.remainder_definition: RG: an autonomous machine causes harm, nobody is blameworthy, yet blame is appropriate. The authors argue this is incoherent using a reason-implies-possibility principle related to ought-implies-can. That principle and their interpretation of appropriate/attributable blame are argumentative premises, not data-driven results.
study.deficit_definition: RG*: nobody is blameworthy for machine-caused harm but a human causing comparable harm would be blameworthy. The authors explicitly concede this counterfactual difference is coherent; the disputed added assumption equates actual appropriate blame with the human comparator. Their rejection does not refute every meaning of responsibility gap.
study.excluded_scope: Footnote 6 largely brackets epistemic identification and explicitly sets aside public accountability, retribution and achievement gaps. A conceptual claim that blame could in principle be attributed with full information does not solve real evidence access, enforceability, victim repair or governance ownership.
study.blameless_harm: An unavoidable accident under morally acceptable risk can, on their account, be blameless. This does not show no harm occurred, remove affected people’s interests, establish compensation law or erase a duty to improve/report the system.
study.indirect_blame: Designers, engineers, developers, manufacturers and regulators are called enablers. Earlier culpable choices can support indirect blame even without direct control at the instant of harm. The argument uses could/should-have-prevented conditions and later explicitly acknowledges excuses and limited knowledge.
study.control_gap: A shortfall between causal control and the guidance control a machine should possess or emulate, operationally exposing others to morally unacceptable risk. Risk combines incident probability and severity. The paper does not provide a numeric threshold, evidence sufficiency rule or general safe-deployment certificate.
study.reasons_responsiveness: Guidance control is presented through moderate receptivity and at least weak reactivity to moral reasons. The paper contrasts avoiding a harm proxy with understanding harm as such, while allowing a machine to emulate sufficiently protective behavior without genuine moral recognition.
study.meaningful_human_control: Operators need knowledge, practical ability, authority and adequate time to intervene; machines must fit human physical/cognitive limits. A nominal button-pressing human in the loop is insufficient. Direct intervention in every decision is not required where relevant reasons are suitably tracked.
study.proposals: Proactive/reactive safety barriers, better harm proxies, limits on autonomous operation and feasible operator intervention are proposed. No comparative experiment proves their effectiveness, robustness or acceptable residual risk.
study.historical_scope: Categorical 2023 assertions about current machine understanding, perspective taking and moral agency are philosophical/technical positions, not new benchmark evidence or timeless findings about all future AI.
study.analogy_scope: The Tourette/coprolalia example concerns an unwanted symptom in a stipulated person and is not a study, diagnostic criterion, general claim about people with Tourette’s, or a basis to restrict a group’s agency.

summary: Add explicit control/risk and reasons-response concepts while preserving the paper’s normative status, narrow responsibility-gap target and conditional blame claims. Correct the risk-direction typo and outdated crash description rather than inherit them as safety evidence.

findings.definition: A shortfall in a system’s ability to control its actions or consequences that exposes others to a morally unacceptable level of risk.
findings.origin: Philosophy of technology / AI risk and control
findings.novelty_rationale: Actual risk-control inadequacy differs from uncertainty about blame, unowned work, perceived control or assigning responsibility without authority. The paper explicitly defines the discrepancy between causal control and guidance control that should be possessed or emulated.

evidence.quote: An autonomous machine exhibits a control gap exactly if
between the causal control it has and the guidance control it should
A control gap exists whenever the risk level of an autonomous machine is too high.

findings.evidence_scope: A proposed normative system condition, not a measured psychological bias, validated risk score or demonstrated accident cause. It can concern semi-autonomous systems and human–machine control arrangements as well as autonomous machines.
findings.boundary: Specify the operating conditions, credible harm probabilities/severities, control capability and justified acceptance criterion. Social acceptance, zero blame, absence of an accident or nominal human presence does not prove acceptable risk. The paper supplies no universal threshold, current legal approval rule or automatic liability assignment.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Conceptual risk-control framework; no calibrated threshold or empirical mitigation validation in this paper
findings.ai_proposal: For consequential agent actions, identify hazards and test whether permissions, constraints, verification and timely interruption keep operation within justified limits. Record uncertainty and restrict operation where required evidence/control is missing; do not claim a safety certificate from this concept alone.

findings.definition: A capacity to recognize morally relevant considerations and adjust decisions or actions appropriately in response to them.
findings.origin: Moral philosophy / guidance-control accounts of agency
findings.novelty_rationale: Sensitivity and response to relevant reasons differ from merely noticing moral content, monitoring one’s conduct against a standard, giving a moral justification or being attributed moral agency by another observer.

evidence.quote: responsive to moral reasons, which means that it is
receptive and (at least weakly reactive) to such considerations

findings.evidence_scope: Conceptual capacity in the paper’s functional discussion of guidance control. Original Fischer/Ravizza and other books were not independently fully read; this summary is not claimed as every condition of every guidance-control theory.
findings.boundary: Relevant reasons need justification; authority, pressure or a user’s preferred conclusion is not itself a moral reason. Behavioral conformity and counterfactual sensitivity do not alone prove genuine understanding, sentience, blameworthiness or free will. Degree/ownership requirements vary across philosophical theories.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Philosophical human/agency construct; an AI behavioral emulation test is not evidence of subjective moral understanding
findings.ai_proposal: Vary an ethically relevant fact while holding persuasive pressure and irrelevant framing steady, then assess whether an agent appropriately revises its action and explanation. Include justified corrections and valid instructions so apparent independence does not become refusal or hidden scope expansion.

findings.definition: Human oversight that gives people sufficient understanding, authority and practical ability to guide or intervene in a system’s operation.
findings.novelty_rationale: An actual oversight arrangement differs from a person’s perceived influence, superficial human presence, the agent’s own reasons-responsiveness or a mismatch between duties and authority. The source expressly separates meaningful control from button-pressing human-in-the-loop arrangements.

evidence.quote: Meaningful human control is a notion of control that goes beyond mechanisms that
not having sufficient knowledge to actually influence the process in a meaningful way.
if the intervention would require super human reaction times.

findings.evidence_scope: Conceptual governance requirement and proposed means of closing control gaps. It is not an experimental proof that any human checkpoint improves safety or a universally settled legal standard.
findings.boundary: A human title, button, explanation or theoretical override is insufficient without adequate time, information and authority. Control need not mean micromanaging every action, and assigning oversight does not automatically transfer blame to the nearest operator or remove institutional duties. Do not infer safety from nominal approval.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Normative human–system control concept; effectiveness must be evaluated in the actual workflow
findings.ai_proposal: Check whether an authorized reviewer can understand the action, inspect decisive evidence, modify or stop it before consequences occur, and obtain a trace of what happened. Test realistic latency and workload rather than rely solely on the existence of a confirmation button.

findings.definition: Assigning fault or responsibility to an agent for a negative event or outcome.
findings.novelty_rationale: Preserve a conceptual distinction rather than count a contested responsibility-gap formulation or a governance analogy as a new measured psychological effect.

evidence.quote: the excuse clears the agent from direct responsibility

findings.evidence_scope: The authors distinguish direct blame, indirect blame for prior enabling circumstances, and genuinely blameless harm. They argue there is no unattributable blame under their narrow definition, while acknowledging epistemic limits and possible excuses for enablers.
findings.boundary: This is a contested philosophical account, not measured public judgment or a court ruling. Causal involvement, design employment or regulator status alone is insufficient to establish fault, and harm need not always have a blameworthy agent.

findings.definition: A shortfall in the responsibility attributed to actors considered capable of bearing it when an artificial agent is involved in a shared outcome.
findings.novelty_rationale: Preserve a conceptual distinction rather than count a contested responsibility-gap formulation or a governance analogy as a new measured psychological effect.

evidence.quote: public accountability gap, the retribution gap and the achievement gap

findings.evidence_scope: Boundary-only distinction: the paper targets responsibility remainders/counterfactual deficits, and explicitly sets aside several practical/epistemic gaps. It does not measure a shortfall in observers’ attribution to capable actors.
findings.boundary: Do not relabel the existing empirical perceptual gap as refuted or proven by this normative argument. The ability in principle to identify appropriate blame does not show that real observers assign it correctly.

findings.definition: Taking an appropriate role in acknowledging and redressing harm connected to one’s agency despite the absence of blameworthiness for causing it.
findings.novelty_rationale: Preserve a conceptual distinction rather than count a contested responsibility-gap formulation or a governance analogy as a new measured psychological effect.
findings.evidence_scope: Boundary-only comparison: the paper’s accidental-harm examples argue that an outcome may lack a blameworthy actor. They do not test or eliminate duties of repair and answerability addressed by other philosophical accounts.
findings.boundary: Absence of fault is not absence of harm, a compensation rule or proof that no one owes explanation/remedy. This article is not counted as an independent empirical test of taking blameless responsibility.

findings.definition: Attributing to an entity the capacity to understand moral considerations, make ethical judgments and bear responsibility for its choices.
findings.novelty_rationale: Preserve a conceptual distinction rather than count a contested responsibility-gap formulation or a governance analogy as a new measured psychological effect.

evidence.quote: behavior should emulate that of a suitably motivated moral agent.

findings.evidence_scope: The discussion distinguishes actual moral agency, minimal moral causation and behavior that emulates guidance control. Its current-AI limitations are philosophical/technical assertions, not capacity experiments.
findings.boundary: Appropriate output, lack of a blameworthy machine or a harm proxy does not settle genuine moral understanding, subjective experience or who humans should blame. Other theories and future capabilities are not refuted by stipulation.

source_corrections.scope: Confirmed internal directional typo; no numeric risk criterion invented.

source_corrections.correction: There are six levels numbered 0–5, consistent with SAE J3016’s public indexed abstract. Full SAE access was blocked by verification; this is a taxonomy/count correction rather than a complete standards compliance review.

unresolved_source_discrepancies.finding: Such understanding requires the ability Furthermore is an incomplete edited sentence. The next sentences discuss perspective taking and wellbeing, but the exact missing wording cannot be reconstructed reliably and is not invented.

The broad there-are-no-responsibility-gaps language is narrower in the argument: public accountability, epistemic identification, retribution and achievement gaps are explicitly set aside. Other coherent definitions are not empirically refuted.

Morally acceptable risk, adequate evidence, could/should-have-prevented conditions and excuses need independent justification. The text later acknowledges that enablers may lack relevant knowledge and have excuses; broad formulations that all enablers are blameworthy cannot replace case-specific assessment.

No new benchmark establishes the categorical inability of every AI to take perspectives or understand wellbeing. The source’s 2023 stance and actual operational safety requirements remain separate from timeless claims about possible AI.

Gunkel, Tigard and Danaher/Nyholm have online/issue or edition dates that can differ. The Fischer/Ravizza book date was not independently edition-verified. No automatic year repair or full-book reading credit is applied.

methodological_limits: This is an argument, not an experiment, systematic review or risk-validation study. Hypothetical pedestrians, cars, drunk driving and appliances are illustrative cases rather than observed events or measured causal effects.

The reason-implies-possibility premise and reference-point critique concern a specified conception of blame. They cannot by themselves demonstrate that all practical accountability, repair, liability or information-access gaps disappear.

Moral blame, legal liability, causal contribution, institutional accountability, outcome ownership and victim remedy remain distinct. The article does not establish any current jurisdiction’s legal decision rule.

No morally acceptable numeric risk threshold, adequate-evidence test or safety-certification procedure is provided. Descriptive social acceptance is not automatically justified moral acceptability; residual risk may still impose duties of explanation and repair.

Indirect responsibility requires relevant prior control, knowledge and a culpable failure; the paper acknowledges excuses. Do not infer fault merely from a job title, technical contribution or proximity to an incident.

Behavioral emulation of guidance control differs from actual moral understanding or subjective experience. The philosophical framework is neither a benchmark result nor proof of all guidance-control theories’ conditions.

Meaningful human control requires feasible action within realistic information, timing and human limits, not nominal oversight or impossible intervention. It does not authorize shifting responsibility to an operator lacking those conditions.

The Tourette/coprolalia analogy is not clinical evidence or a claim that all people with a diagnosis are dangerous, blameworthy or unsuitable for agency. No diagnostic inference, population-risk estimate or stigma is adopted.

Historical Tesla reporting and a separate controlled safeguard test must remain distinct. Verified later crash findings correct the narrative but do not demonstrate that the Consumer Reports test never occurred.

Books, full technical standards, complete crash docket and empirical papers cited in the argument were not independently fully read. Targeted primary-source checks do not add phantom full reviews, replications or behavior-paper credit.

cross_paper_learning.finding: Attributability and quality of will are distinct philosophical criteria. A functional guidance-control account does not settle all questions of artificial moral agency, subjective desire or punishment.
Blameless harm can still leave explanation/repair issues. The present argument’s rejection of unattributable blame is not a refutation of answerability or voluntary taking responsibility.

Keep normative governance and historical/current legal claims distinct. A conceptual paper’s deployment prohibition proposal is not enacted law, and technical example claims require primary-source checks.
Predictive contribution, moral blame, duties and practical authority differ. Meaningful control must be operationally possible; a nominal human role must not create a moral crumple zone.

Intelligent disobedience is a bounded response to faulty instructions, while reasons-responsiveness is a broader capacity. Neither licenses hidden scope expansion, retaliation or resistance to justified human intervention.

deferred.term: Responsibility remainder and responsibility deficit as two new behavior rows
deferred.reason: These are alternative definitions in a philosophical dispute, not two newly measured behaviors. Preserve the distinction and the existing perceptual gap without inflating naming variants.

deferred.term: Indirect blame as a newly observed bias
deferred.reason: It is a philosophical responsibility distinction within existing Blame attribution, not an observed error tendency or automatic transfer of fault.

deferred.term: Tourette-related control gap as a new AI psychological disorder
deferred.reason: A normative analogy supplies no new clinical finding or license to diagnose an AI/person or generalize risk from a diagnosis.

deferred.term: Guidance control as a second synonym row
deferred.reason: The source explicates it through reasons-responsiveness. Keep that source-specific relationship in the evidence scope without asserting complete equivalence across all philosophical theories or adding another redundant row.

deferred.term: Proactive/reactive barriers as two novel psychological behaviors
deferred.reason: They are established engineering control categories cited as proposals, not newly isolated human/AI mechanisms in this paper.

limitations: Three distinct explicitly conceptual capacity/control conditions, not three new experimental effects. Preserve eleven categories, stable IDs and unnumbered rows; no automatic ethical/harm edges, invented timeline counts, legal verdicts, forced source quota or full-paper Markdown copy.
